abstract.text: A directed hypergraph: a finite set of vertices and a finite collection of hyperedges, each an
ordered pair of vertex sets, its sources (tail) and its targets (head).

inlineContent.text: Gallo, Longo, Pallottino and Nguyen (“Directed hypergraphs and applications”,
42(2–3):177–201, 1993) define a hyperarc as an ordered pair of disjoint, possibly
empty, vertex sets. Here either side may be empty, and a vertex may be on both sides, which is
the hypergraph form of a self-loop.
